text: The correct sequence of reagents used in the preparation of 4-bromo-2-nitroethyl benzene from benzene is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The target is ethylbenzene carrying $-\mathrm{NO}{}_{2}$ ortho (C-2) and Br para (C-4) to the ethyl group.

The ethyl group is introduced as an acetyl group by Friedel–Crafts acylation ($\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{COCl}/\mathrm{AlCl}{}_{3}$) and then reduced to $-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$ by Clemmensen reduction ($\mathrm{Zn}-\mathrm{Hg}/\mathrm{HCl}$), which avoids the rearrangement and polysubstitution of direct alkylation.

Ethyl is ortho/para-directing, so bromination ($\mathrm{Br}{}_{2}/\mathrm{AlBr}{}_{3}$) gives mainly 4-bromoethylbenzene.

On nitration ($\mathrm{HNO}{}_{3}/\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{SO}{}_{4}$), the activating ethyl group directs $-\mathrm{NO}{}_{2}$ ortho to itself (C-2), giving 4-bromo-2-nitroethylbenzene:


[IMG]

In (A) and (C) the meta-directing acetyl group is still present during substitution and $\mathrm{Zn}/\mathrm{HCl}$ also reduces $-\mathrm{NO}{}_{2}$; in (D) nitrobenzene does not undergo Friedel–Crafts acylation.

Hence, the correct option is (B).

text:
The solubility of $Ca(OH)_{2}$ in water is :

[Given : The solubility product of $Ca(OH)_{2}$ in water = 5.5 $\times$ $10^{-6}$]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let, solubility of $Ca(OH)_{2}$ in pure water = S mol/L

$Ca(OH)_{2}$ $⇌$ $Ca^{2+}_{Smol/L}+2OH^{-}_{2\times S(mol/L)}$

$K_{sp} =$ [$Ca^{2+}$] [$OH^{-}$]$^{2} = S$ $\times$ $(2S)^{2} = 4 S^{3} ($mol/L)

The expression of $K_{sp}$ can also be written as,

$K_{sp} = x^{x} . y^{y} . S^{x + y}$

$= 1^{1} . 2^{2} . S^{1 + 2}$

$= 4 S^{3}$ [$\because$ For $Ca(OH)_{2}$ : x = 1, y = 2]

x and y are the coefficients of cations and anions respectively

$S=\left (\frac{K_{sp}}{4}\right )^{1/3}=\left (\frac{5.5\times 10^{-6}}{4}\right )^{1/3}$

$=1.11\times 10^{-2}$ ml/L

the expected angles of $120^{o}$ and $180^{o}$ respectively. Here axial and equatorial both bonds are present. And we know axial bonds are longer and weaker.

text:
In which of the following order the given complex ions are arranged correctly with respect to their decreasing spin only magnetic moment?

(i) [FeF$_{6}$]$^{3-}$

(ii) [$Co(NH_{3})_{6}$]$^{3+}$

(iii) [NiCl$_{4}$]$^{2-}$

(iv) [$Cu(NH_{3})_{4}$]$^{2+}$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Spin-only $μ=\sqrt{n(n+2)}$ BM increases with the number of unpaired electrons $n$.

(i) $[\mathrm{FeF}{}_{6}]{}^{3-}$: $\mathrm{Fe}{}^{3+}$ is $3d^{5}$ and $\mathrm{F}{}^{-}$ is weak-field, so no pairing occurs (outer-orbital $sp^{3}d^{2}$) and $n=5$.


[IMG]

(ii) $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}){}_{6}]{}^{3+}$: $\mathrm{Co}{}^{3+}$ is $3d^{6}$ and $\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}$ pairs all six electrons ($t_{2g}^{6}e_{g}^{0}$, inner-orbital $d^{2}sp^{3}$), so $n=0$.


[IMG]

(iii) $[\mathrm{NiCl}{}_{4}]{}^{2-}$: $\mathrm{Ni}{}^{2+}$ is $3d^{8}$ and weak-field $\mathrm{Cl}{}^{-}$ gives tetrahedral $sp^{3}$ with two unpaired electrons, so $n=2$.


[IMG]

(iv) $[\mathrm{Cu}(\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}){}_{4}]{}^{2+}$: $\mathrm{Cu}{}^{2+}$ is $3d^{9}$ and the complex is square planar ($dsp^{2}$); nine d electrons always leave one unpaired, so $n=1$.

The moments are (i) $5.92$, (iii) $2.83$, (iv) $1.73$ and (ii) $0$ BM, so the order is (i) > (iii) > (iv) > (ii).

Hence, the correct option is (C).

text:
Given below are two statements :

Statement I : The identification of $Ni^{2+}$ is carried out by dimethyl glyoxime in the presence of $NH_{4}OH$. 

Statement II : The dimethyl glyoxime is a bidentate neutral ligand.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Statement I is true. Dimethyl glyoxime (DMG) is a chelating reagent commonly used for the identification of $Ni^{2+}$ ions in aqueous solution. In the presence of ammonium hydroxide $(NH_{4}OH), Ni^{2+}$ reacts with dimethyl glyoxime to form a deep red-colored complex, which can be used to confirm the presence of $Ni^{2+}$ ions.

Statement II is also true. Dimethyl glyoxime is a neutral bidentate ligand, which means it has two donor atoms that can coordinate with a metal ion, and its overall charge is neutral.


[IMG]

text: The correct order of bond dissociation enthalpy of halogens is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Bond dissociation enthalpies of the halogens (in $\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$): $\mathrm{Cl}{}_{2}$ 242.6, $\mathrm{Br}{}_{2}$ 192.8, $\mathrm{F}{}_{2}$ 158.8 and $\mathrm{I}{}_{2}$ 151.1.

From $\mathrm{Cl}{}_{2}$ to $\mathrm{I}{}_{2}$ the atomic size increases, the bond becomes longer and the orbital overlap poorer, so the bond enthalpy decreases: $\mathrm{Cl}{}_{2}>\mathrm{Br}{}_{2}>\mathrm{I}{}_{2}$.

$\mathrm{F}{}_{2}$ is anomalous: the F–F bond is very short, so the lone pairs on the two small fluorine atoms repel each other strongly and weaken the bond, placing $\mathrm{F}{}_{2}$ below $\mathrm{Br}{}_{2}$ but still above $\mathrm{I}{}_{2}$.

$\mathrm{Cl}{}_{2}>\mathrm{Br}{}_{2}>\mathrm{F}{}_{2}>\mathrm{I}{}_{2}$

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th February Evening Shift

text:
Copper reduces NO${}_{3}^{-}$ into NO and $NO_{2}$ depending upon the concentration of HNO$_{3}$ in solution. (Assuming fixed [$Cu^{2+}$] and $P_{$NO$} = P_{$NO$}_{2})$, the HNO$_{3}$ concentration at which the thermodynamic tendency for reduction of NO${}_{3}^{-}$ into NO and $NO_{2}$ by copper is same is $10^{x} M$. The value of 2x is $_______. ($Rounded off to the nearest integer)

[Given, $E_{Cu^{2+}/Cu}^{o}=0.34$ V, $E_{NO_{3}^{-}/NO}^{o}=0.96$ V, $E_{NO_{3}^{-}/NO_{2}}^{o}=0.79$ V and at 298 K, $\frac{RT}{F}$(2.303) = 0.059]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Both reductions share the same copper half-cell, so their thermodynamic tendencies are equal when the two nitrate electrode potentials are equal. Take $[\mathrm{H}{}^{+}]=[\mathrm{NO}{}_{3}{}^{-}]=c$ from $\mathrm{HNO}{}_{3}$ and $p_{\mathrm{NO}}=p_{\mathrm{NO}{}_{2}}=1\text{bar}$.

For $\mathrm{NO}{}_{3}{}^{-}+4\mathrm{H}{}^{+}+3\mathrm{e}{}^{-}\longrightarrow \mathrm{NO}+2\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$:

$E_{1}=0.96-\dfrac{0.059}{3}\log \dfrac{1}{c\cdot c^{4}}=0.96+\dfrac{5\times 0.059}{3}\log c$

For $\mathrm{NO}{}_{3}{}^{-}+2\mathrm{H}{}^{+}+\mathrm{e}{}^{-}\longrightarrow \mathrm{NO}{}_{2}+\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$:

$E_{2}=0.79-0.059\log \dfrac{1}{c\cdot c^{2}}=0.79+3\times 0.059\log c$

Setting $E_{1}=E_{2}$:

$0.17=0.059\left (3-\dfrac{5}{3}\right )\log c=0.0787\log c\Rightarrow \log c=2.16$

So $[\mathrm{HNO}{}_{3}]=10^{2.16}\text{M}$, $x=2.16$ and $2x=4.32\approx 4$.

Hence, the answer is 4.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th February Evening Shift

text:
If a compound AB dissociates to the extent of 75% in an aqueous solution, the molality of the solution which shows a 2.5 K rise in the boiling point of the solution is $____________$ molal. (Rounded off to the nearest integer)

[$K_{b} = 0.52 K kg$ mol$^{-1}$]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
As AB is a binary electrolyte,

$\therefore$ AB $⇌$ $A^{+} + B^{-}, n = 2$

$i=1+α(n-1)=1+\frac{75}{100}(2-1)=1.75$

Given, $\DeltaT_{b} = 2.5 K$

$K_{b} = 0.52 K kg$ mol$^{-1}$

$\therefore$ $\DeltaT_{b} = K_{b}$ $\times$ m $\times$ i

$\Rightarrow m=\frac{\Delta T_{b}}{K_{b}\times i}=\frac{2.5}{0.52\times 1.75}$

$=2.74\simeq 3$ mol/kg
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th February Evening Shift

text:

= 180600 J mol$^{-1} = 180.6 kJ$ mol$^{-1}$ $\simeq$ 181 kJ mol$^{-1}$

text:
Consider titration of NaOH solution versus 1.25 M oxalic acid solution. At the end point following burette readings were obtained.

(i) 4.5 mL

(ii) 4.5 mL

(iii) 4.4 mL

(iv) 4.4 mL

(v) 4.4 mL

If the volume of oxalic acid taken was 10.0 mL then the molarity of the NaOH solution is $________ M. ($Rounded off to the nearest integer)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Average burette reading = Volume of NaOH solution $(V_{1})$

$=\frac{4.5+4.5+4.4+4.4+4.4}{5}$

= 4.44 mL

Strength of NaOH solution $= S_{1}(M) ($say$) = S_{1}(N)$

Volume of oxalic acid solution $(V_{2}) = 10 mL$

Strength of oxalic acid solution $(S_{2}) = 1.25 M = 1.25$ $\times$ 2 N

So, $V_{1}S_{1}=V_{2}S_{2}$ ($\because$ Law of equivalence)

$\Rightarrow S_{1}=\frac{V_{2}S_{2}}{V_{1}}=\frac{10\times (1.25\times 2)}{4.44}=5.63$ N

$\simeq 6M=6M$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th February Evening Shift

text: Five moles of an ideal gas at 293 K is expanded isothermally from an initial pressure of 2.1 MPa to 1.3 MPa against at constant external pressure 4.3 MPa. The heat transferred in this process is $_________ kJ$ mol$^{-1}. ($Rounded off to the nearest integer) [Use R = 8.314 J mol$^{-1}K^{-1}$]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The gas performs isothermal irreversible work (W).

where, $\Delta$U = 0 (change in internal energy)

From, 1st law of thermodynamics,

$\Rightarrow$ $\Delta$U = $\Delta$Q + W

$\Rightarrow$ 0 = $\Delta$Q + W

$\Rightarrow$ $\Delta$Q = $-$W

Now, $W=-p_{ext}(V_{2}-V_{1})$

$=-p_{ext}\left (\frac{nRT}{p_{2}}-\frac{nRT}{p_{1}}\right )=-p_{ext}\times nRT\left (\frac{1}{p_{2}}-\frac{1}{p_{1}}\right )$

Given, $p_{$ext} = 4.3 MPa, $p_{1} = 2.1$ MPa, $p_{2} = 1.3$ MPa, n = 5 mol, T = 293 K and R = 8.314 J mol$^{-1} K^{-1}$

$=-4.3\times 5\times 8.314\times 293\left (\frac{1}{1.3}-\frac{1}{2.1}\right )$

= $-$ 15347.70 J mol$^{-1}$

= $-$ 15.347 kJ mol$^{-1}$ $\simeq$ $-$ 15 kJ mol$^{-1}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\Delta$Q = 15 kJ mol$^{-1}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th February Evening Shift

The rate constant of a reaction increases by five times on increase in temperature from 27${}^{\circ }$C to 52${}^{\circ }$C. The value of activation energy in kJ mol$^{-1}$ is $_________. ($Rounded off to the nearest integer)

[$R = 8.314 J K^{-1}$mol$^{-1}$]

text:
Among the following, number of metal/s which can be used as electrodes in the photoelectric cell is $_________. ($Integer answer)

(A) Li

(B) Na

(C) Rb

(D) Cs
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
A photoelectric-cell electrode must emit electrons readily when light falls on it, which needs a very low ionisation enthalpy.

Caesium has the lowest ionisation enthalpy among the alkali metals ($376\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$) and is used, along with potassium, as the electrode in photoelectric cells; Li, Na and Rb are not used.

Among Li, Na, Rb and Cs, only Cs qualifies, so the number of such metals is 1.

Hence, the answer is 1.
